name: Projected Interpolation Degree of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, every projection has one trace and interpolation degree zero. For $n\ge2$, the full projection consists of the $n$ singletons, on which $\sum_i a_i x_i$ interpolates arbitrary values $a_i$. A proper projection onto $S$ consists of the empty trace and the singletons in $S$; values $a_0,a_i$ are interpolated by $a_0+\sum_{i\in S}(a_i-a_0)x_i$, including $S=\emptyset$. Thus every projection has interpolation degree at most one, while the full class has two distinct concepts and needs degree at least one.
